_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Evolving a database schema over time without breaking deployed application code — the expand/contract pattern,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "design the expand-contract sequence to rename a column from `name` to `full_name` across a deployed system"
cases.context: The agent has access to the schema-evolution skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is schema-evolution the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes schema-evolution as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against transaction-isolation, entity-relationship-modeling, database-migration
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the schema-evolution workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore schema-evolution
Does not route to transaction-isolation, entity-relationship-modeling, database-migration when the schema-evolution scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
